scope: Independent holistic offline native park review of exact v006 bytes against all three photographic sources and conservatory-v013 native clay quality. All earlier failures are preserved. Pass is limited to native clay visual quality.

closed_findings.resolution: Willow tunnel now has substantial physical leafy side and roof cover. Open portal and the play shelter identity are readable in plot_walk and walk.
Stepping faces are broad and flat; stone footprints and bank widths vary. Mixed perimeter clusters reduce the bead-row appearance. Octagonal simplification is compatible with this clay tier.

Three overlapping leafy beds connect the deck/stream, tunnel flank and sand corner. They now read as planted masses at aerial and pedestrian scale, and visible hedge end faces have leaf cover. Broader right/rear crown hierarchy from v004 remains intact.

The sand-corner tree now has a coherent broad crown with irregular kit-quality foliage covering the exposed radial scaffold. Hanging outer branchlets remain visible in rear/detail and preserve a drooping silhouette. It fits the neighboring native trees.

positive_findings: Whole-scene composition reads as a nature-play garden with stream, log play, sand, leafy tunnel and raised tree deck.
Widened right/rear crowns, low connected plant masses and a drooping sand-corner tree create distinct landscape layers.
Willow tunnel has leafy sides and roof while preserving open portals.
Flat stepping surfaces and mixed-size banks support the source-specific stream programme.
Bridge, rope structures, deck/stairs, benches and foliage have coherent visible contacts.
Side walking route and both end connections remain visibly clear.
All whole-scene images retain complete bounds and margins; pedestrian views show physical leaves, furnishings and ground detail consistent with the native catalogue tier.

nonblocking_notes.finding: Stepping stones and woven tunnel remain stylized; more natural rock silhouettes and varied branchlet spacing would be optional polish within this native clay tier.
Phone-front pairs the pedestrian source with an aerial render. Full walk and plot_walk images were separately inspected.

benchmark.assessment: At native clay tier, the park now has coherent authored ground planting, differentiated canopy, physical foreground detail and source-specific programme. The conservatory has a deliberately denser botanical programme; equal flower coverage is not required for nature play. No remaining P0/P1 visual deficit is identified.
